headline: Keep source families separate.
copy: Every answer should know what family it is standing in before it explains anything.

fields.name: family
fields.why: Prevents calling every Hindu text Veda.

fields.name: status
fields.why: Separates answer-ready, review-needed, and source-gap lanes.

fields.name: reviewRole
fields.why: Names who should review the family before expansion.

fields.name: boundary
fields.why: Keeps text, tradition, analogy, and modern claims distinct.

records.title: Steady action
records.summary: Supports a calm reflection on steady action while keeping outcomes and personal identity separate.
records.boundary: Reflection support only; not therapy, medical advice, ritual instruction, or spiritual command.

records.title: Oppenheimer source correction
records.summary: Corrects the common category confusion: the famous line is associated with the Gita, not the four Vedas.
records.boundary: Do not call it a direct quote from the four Vedas.

records.title: Gayatri mantra review candidate
records.summary: High-value source candidate that must stay in review until Sanskrit, recitation, and rights posture are stronger.
records.boundary: No ritual instruction, initiation advice, or pronunciation authority.

records.title: Renunciation and stewardship candidate
records.summary: Useful for desire, possession, and restraint questions, but it needs commentary notes before learner-facing simplification.
records.boundary: Do not flatten the verse into productivity advice or wealth advice.

records.title: Self-knowledge humility candidate
records.summary: Potentially useful for humility and self-knowledge boundaries, but requires tradition-aware commentary.
records.boundary: Do not promise realization, status, or spiritual attainment.

records.title: Gita classification
records.summary: Helps explain that the Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata and is usually classified as Smriti.
records.boundary: Use for classification only; do not overstate sectarian consensus.

records.title: Devotion story candidate
records.summary: Can help with story-based devotion questions after source edition and interpretation boundaries are added.
records.boundary: Do not present story material as direct Vedic statement.

records.title: Commentary lens candidate
records.summary: Needed for interpretation differences, but must stay separate from source text and modern analogy.
records.boundary: Never collapse commentary into the base verse.

example.allowedUse: classification, direct citation packet, calm reflection
example.notAllowed: calling it direct Veda, ritual authority, medical or spiritual prescription

rules.title: Do not merge families
rules.copy: A Gita answer must not become a Veda answer for convenience.

rules.title: Commentary is a layer
rules.copy: Commentary may explain the source but should not replace it.

rules.title: Uncertain is allowed
rules.copy: A thin source family can be marked uncertain without shame.
